programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Nuair tha Beag Chlangair a-muigh ’g iasgach air an long-chiùil, tha e a' glacadh rudeigin. Ach dè th’ann? When Beag Chlangair is out fishing on the music boat, he catches something. But what is it?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Nuair tha na Clangairean ag argamaid mu cò as luaithe, tha ‘ad ri rèiseadh ’son dearbhadh cò as luaithe - ach tha cuideigin ri foill! When the Clangers argue about who is faster, they race to determine who indeed it is, but someone is cheating!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona a' cur seachad an latha a' leantainn na faoileagan 's ag ionnsachadh ioma rud inntinneach mun na cleachdaidhean aca... fiosrachadh a tha air leth feumail nuair a thig Baba bochd a chur ann an cunnart! Oona spends the day following the seagulls, learning all sorts of interesting facts about their behaviour. This information comes in very useful when Baba gets himself in a spot of bother!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha tubaist aig Bernie a tha fàgail an t-slige aige briste! Tha Oona 's Silky a' cur romhpa slige ùr a lorg dha aig grunnd na mara ach chan e gnìomh furasta a th' ann dhaibh tè fhreagarrach fhaighinn! When Bernie has an accident and manages to break his shell, Oona and Silky volunteer to dive to the depths to find him a new one. However, it proves to be quite the challenge to find one suitable.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing ‘s Flop air a bhith cluich falach-fead ‘s spòrs uabhasach air a bhith aig Bing - na h-uimhir de spòrs ‘s nach eil e deònach sguir a chluich, fiù ‘s ann am buth Padget… neo gun fhios aig Flop g’ eil an geama fhathast a’ dol! Bing and Flop have been playing hide-and-seek and Bing has been having so much fun that he doesn’t want the game to end, not even when they go to Padget’s shop and Flop has stopped playing!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing a’ togail caisteal-gainmhich ‘s tha Pando a’ tighinn le làraidh bheag spaideal gus cuideachadh a thoirt dha. Ge-tà, tha an làraidh ag adhbharachadh beagan troiblaid dhaibh… agus do sheasmhachd a’ chaisteil…! Bing is building a sandcastle and is joined by Pando, who has brought his toy dumper truck to help with the construction. However, the truck causes some confusion and ends up putting the castle at risk of destruction!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha màthair Pheicein a’ trod ris às dèidh dha a ràdh ri nurs gu bheil a sròn mòr. Bhon mhionaid sin, tha Peicein a’ tòiseachadh ri breugan beaga innse, is tha iad sin a’ sìor fhàs nam breugan mòra, is ag adhbharrachadh mì-thuigse uabhasach! Petit's mum scolds him for telling a nurse that she has a big nose. From that moment on, Petit starts telling white lies that grow little by little, until they turn into big lies and cause a huge misunderstanding.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl a’ coimhead às dèidh Maighstir Gruaman, peata deargain Siùsaidh. Tha na Pluic a’ dèanamh an dìcheall a shàbhaladh às dèidh do Mhial-mhogach ithe. Saoil am faigh iad thuige mus tèid a leaghadh coltach ri biadh, ann an stamag Mhial-mhogaich? The Spuds launch a rescue mission when Fuzzypeg eats the flea that Dave is pet sitting for Lil Sue. Will they reach Mr Grumps before he is dissolved like food inside Fuzzypeg’s tummy?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha droch latha aig Pòl is gun smaoineachadh, ann an agallamh le neach-naidheachd, tha e ag ràdh gu bheil Grodanais cianail. Nuair a tha seo air a shealltainn air na naidheachdan, tha am baile air fad a’ tionndadh na aghaidh. Le cuideachadh bho charaidean agus sionnach, tha Pòl a’ cur chùisean ceart le bhith a’ clàradh bhidio mu dheidhinn na rudan a tha math mun bhaile. Dave has a bad day and tells a news reporter that Grimsby is rubbish. When his words are aired on the news, his whole seaside town turns against him. With the help of his friends and a rogue fox, Dave makes amends by shooting a film about all the great things that Grimsby has to offer.

programme.title: Na Saboteurs
programme.desc: Ten-year-old Magaidh is unhappy that her father has invited the local teacher round for dinner. Her friend Dean meanwhile is trying to pluck up the courage to ask Magaidh to the local dance.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sgrudaire sgoile air nochdadh aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus chan eil Maighstir Mackle neo na tidsearan deiseil air a shon. Chan eil cùisean a’ coimhead ro mhath do Mhaighstir MhicFhraing ach tha Maighstir Strachan air a chasan, neo co-dhiù aona chois a lorg. Dè as urrainn a dhol ceàrr?! There’s a surprise visit from a school inspector at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. It’s not looking good for Mr MacFhraing, although Mr Strachan seems to have found his feet, well one foot at least. What could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo seallaidh i dhut dòigh sgoinneil air coltas eadar-dhealaichte a thoirt air do chuid aodaich! Choirstaidh presents from her studio A’ Chùil to show you a great way of changing up your clothes.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach seachdainn le sgioba-naidheachd BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Raonaid Nic an Fhùcadair, Iain ‘Costello’ MacÌomhair, Rona NicLeòid ‘s Donnchadh MacLeòid, agus an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Moira NicÌomhair a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain. Cuideachd, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek, agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents with a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Rachel Walker, Iain ‘Costello’ Maciver, Rona MacLeod & Duncan MacLeod and the choir Soisgeul, conducted by Gareth Fuller. Moira MacIver reflects on beliefs with selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek, and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Airson a’ chiad uair, tha pàrtaidhean nàiseantach a-nis a’ riaghladh ann an Alba agus ‘sa Chuimrigh, is tha Prìomh Mhinistear Nàiseantach ann an Èirinn a Tuath. Tha Mìcheal MacNèill air a bhith ‘sna trì dùthchannan a’ coinneachdadh ri daoine air gach taobh de dheasbad na bunreachd. For the first time, nationalist parties lead the governments of Scotland and Wales, while Northern Ireland has a nationalist First Minister. Join Michael MacNeil as he travels through the three nations, meeting those on both sides of the constitutional divide.

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: Peter is busy planting more vegetables and he ropes his mum in to help label them. Tha Pàdruig a’cur glasraich is bheir e air a mhàthair sanasan a dhèanamh le na h-ainmean.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Anns an dàrna prògram, tha Kate a’ cumail orra air a turas is i a’ cuairteachadh ceann a deas an eilein, agus ’s ann nas fheàrr a tha na seallaidhean a’ fàs. Bidh i seòladh tro Chaol Reithe ann an cuideachd muc-mhara, a’ dèanamh a slighe sìos fon talamh gu uamh shònraichte agus bidh a’ faighinn cothrom snàmh fo sgàil a’ Chuilthinn. Tha i cuideachd a’ tadhal air caisteal eile aig a bheil ceangal ris a’ bhana-ghaisgeach, Sgathach agus tha i a’ faighinn cothrom snàmh ann an Loch a tha aithnichte mar Loch nan Dùbhraichean. Kate continues her journey around the south end of the Isle of Skye, and the scenery just keeps getting better and better. She sails through Kylerhea in the company of a whale, makes her way underground to a special cave and swims in the shadow of the famous Cuillins. Kate also visits another castle which is said to have strong connections to the warrior queen Sgathach, and she gets an opportunity to swim in Loch nan Dùbhraichean. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, or writing poems, to mindfulness, camper van life or playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Cuirm shònraichte aig Celtic Connections a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de dh’òrain ùra Gàidhlig, le Joy Dunlop. A’ togail air pròiseact Òran Ùr bho BhBC Radio nan Gàidheal a bha a’ taisbeanadh òrain Gàidhlig a chaidh a dhèanamh bho thoiseach na linne, tha a’ chuirm ga chuir air dòigh le Gillebrìde MacIlleMhaoil, le ceòl bho rionnagan seinn agus sgrìobhaidh na Gàidhlig, cuide ri aoighean eile. A special concert at Celtic Connections celebrating 25 years of new Gaelic songs, presented by Joy Dunlop. Building on BBC Radio nan Gàidheal’s Òran Ùr project that showcased Gaelic songs written since the turn of the century, the concert is curated by Gillebride MacMillan. It features performances from stars of Gaelic singing and contemporary songwriting as well as various surprise guests. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Le seusan a’ ghiomaich air fàire, tha na sgiobairean a’ cogadh a’ chadail agus an aimsir gus cuòtathan crùbaige agus creachainn a choileanadh mus ruith an tìde agus an fhortan a-mach orra. With lobster season looming, captains fight fatigue and the elements to fill crab and scallop quotas before time - and luck - run out.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus is joined by long time friend Angus Macmillan as they go fishing off the west coast of Lewis. Leaving Loch Odhairn, they travel south to the lighthouse at the Miolaid where a successful day’s fishing awaits. Against the backdrop of the magical Shiant Islands, they discuss the old-school traditions of island fishing before proving the effectiveness of modern methods, too. Tha deagh charaid Aonghais, Aonghas MacMhaolain, còmhla ris agus iad a’ dol a dh’iasgach far costa siar Leòdhais. A’ fàgail Loch Odhairn, tha iad a’ siubhal gu deas chun taigh-sholais aig a’ Mhiolaid, far a bheil latha soirbheachail air thoiseach orra. Air beulaibh nan Eileanan Mòra, bruidhnidh iad air traidiseanan iasgaich seann-fhasanta nan eilean, mus dearbh iad cho èifeachdach ’s a tha dòighean an latha an-diugh.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: Fish occur in populations of billions and there are over 30,000 species, more than in any other group of backboned animals. The development of the backbone was a crucial advance in evolution - and it probably came from a most unlikely source, a little jelly-like creature called a sea squirt.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of his hero Fridjtof Nansen who, in 1892, announced a daring plan to be first to the North Pole, an idea considered so off-the-wall that no scientist would volunteer to join him on a venture they believed was nothing short of suicide. He allowed his ship to become stuck in the crushing pack ice, hoping it would drift to the Pole, and then set off on foot across the frozen wastes. Nansen became the forefather of polar exploration, inventing practical techniques that today allow people to survive, travel and work in the most hostile and forbidding places on our planet.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: If you think Britain has recently been on the end of some of the worst floods and storms ever experienced, think again. So says solar scientist Dr Lucie Green, as she takes a journey back through our most turbulent and dramatic weather history. She finds an 18th-century storm surge that killed over a thousand people working in open Somerset fields, a hurricane that drowned a fifth of the British Navy and winters so bitter that the country came close to total shutdown. But she also explores how our reactions to killer storms and cruel winters helped forge a weather science that today allows us to predict - and protect ourselves from - the worst extremes.

programme.title: Winterwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham introduces a classic documentary from the BBC's archive, which takes a look at the worst winter of the 20th century in 1963. He also explores what we now know about how this big freeze affected Britain's wildlife, and how it would cope if we experienced another equally bad winter.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: A specially curated night of musical gems, from the Royal Albert Hall. Alongside Beethoven's famous symphony are Mussorgsky's A Night on a Bare Mountain and Strauss' Don Juan. Presented by Petroc Trelawny and Georgia Mann and featuring performances by the BBC Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Marin Alsop and Elim Chan.

programme.title: A303: Highway to the Sun
programme.desc: The A303 is the road that passes Stonehenge on the way to the beaches of Devon and Cornwall. On the way, it whisks drivers through 5,000 years of remarkable moments in British history. And it is the star of this film made for armchair travellers and history lovers. Writer Tom Fort drives its 92-mile length in a lovingly restored Morris Traveller. Along the way, he has many adventures - he digs up the 1960s master plan for the A303's dreams of superhighway status, and meets up with a Neolithic traveller who knew the road like the back of his hand. He also gets to know a section of the Roman 303, uncovers a medieval murder mystery and discovers what lies at the end of the Highway to the Sun.

programme.title: Hans Zimmer: Hollywood Rebel
programme.desc: The story of one of the most celebrated and sought-after movie composers, as told by the man himself and his closest collaborators. Across a glittering 40-year career, Hans has redefined the movie score, thrilling audiences, pioneering new techniques and introducing new generations to the drama of orchestral music. In this portrait, Hans reveals the musical secrets of his craft - how he goes about terrifying, moving and raising an audience's spirits through his music.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI can write, code, plan and problem-solve in seconds. But as we hand more tasks over to machines, what happens to our own skills? In this episode, AI Decoded investigates whether AI is enhancing human intelligence or quietly eroding it. From doctors and software engineers to students growing up with AI tutors, we explore new research suggesting that reliance on AI could affect critical thinking, expertise and decision-making. Joining Marc are leading paediatric neurosurgeon Owase Jeelani, digital transformation researcher Dr Tapani Rinta-Kahila and AI Decoded co-host Dr Stephanie Hare.

Alastair Sooke travels from north to south, to examine ancient paintings and visits surviving historic gardens. His aim is to understand how Chinese aesthetics and philosophy are reflected in the design of traditional gardens.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The Trump administration has issued subpoenas to several New York Times journalists following reporting about alleged security concerns involving President Trump's new Air Force One, a plane donated by Qatar. The case has prompted debate over the balance between protecting national security and safeguarding press freedom. Claire Atkinson, founder of The Media Mix newsletter, outlines the latest developments. The BBC's latest annual report comes as the corporation warns that public service media is facing a period of jeopardy. The figures show a further fall in licence fee-paying households, alongside changing audience habits and continued financial pressures as charter renewal negotiations continue. Rhodri Talfan Davies, the BBC's deputy director-general, sets out the corporation's position. Broadcaster and author Iain Dale reflects on a career spanning politics, publishing, blogging and radio following the publication of his memoir Have I Said Too Much?. The interview covers the enduring appeal of the radio phone-in, the influence of social media on broadcasting, and changing relationships between politicians and traditional media.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: Aled Jones is in the historic city of Hull to explore how music, culture and faith are bringing new life to this historic city, resulting in it being named one of the top places in the world to visit in 2026. Aled goes to Hull Minster and learns from musical director Mark Keith how its choir was saved ten years ago and is now thriving, partly due to an innovative partnership that takes music into local primary schools to spread the joy of singing. Aled also visits the workshop of Helen Richardson, who transforms old or discarded items into treasure, all inspired by God’s restorative powers. And Aled joins a remarkable local church that meets in its own adventure park, complete with high rope courses and zip wires! He hears from Minister Jarrod Cooper how the facilities help promote fun, family and a sense of community. With glorious music, including some specially recorded hymns from a packed Hull Minster: 1. Hark, My Soul, It Is yhe Lord – Hull Minster 2. A Gaelic Blessing – Hull Minster 3. Holy Forever – Way Church, Wigan 4. O Thou Who Camest from Above – Hull Minster 5. King of Kings, Majesty – The Mint Methodist Church, Exeter 6. How Great Thou Art – Hull Minster

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Ginny Buckley’s buyer today is chasing an inspiring landscape. She wants a new Carmarthenshire home that has as much land as her £450,000 budget can muster. She’s also keen to make some green-fingered, like-minded friends in the area, so a trip to meet some volunteers at the National Garden of Wales is also on the agenda.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita continues her east coast road trip, visiting the Naze, a nature reserve on the Essex coast. Here, coastal erosion is particularly severe, with around 2 to 3 metres lost from the cliffs every year. But there are benefits to a crumbling coastline – it can reveal 55 million years of history. Anita joins a group of enthusiastic fossil hunters on the lookout for remnants of the coast's fascinating past. She also discovers what has been done to protect the area’s heritage and visits one of over a thousand brightly coloured beach huts overlooking the North Sea. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the hidden histories found across our landscape.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: Aled Jones is in the historic city of Hull to explore how music, culture and faith are bringing new life to this historic city, resulting in it being named one of the top places in the world to visit in 2026. Aled goes to Hull Minster and learns from musical director Mark Keith how its choir was saved ten years ago and is now thriving, partly due to an innovative partnership that takes music into local primary schools to spread the joy of singing. Aled also visits the workshop of Helen Richardson, who transforms old or discarded items into treasure, all inspired by God’s restorative powers. And Aled joins a remarkable local church that meets in its own adventure park, complete with high rope courses and zip wires! He hears from Minister Jarrod Cooper how the facilities help promote fun, family and a sense of community. With glorious music, including some specially recorded hymns from a packed Hull Minster: 1. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: Aled Jones is in the historic city of Hull to explore how music, culture and faith are bringing new life to this historic city, resulting in it being named one of the top places in the world to visit in 2026. Aled goes to Hull Minster and learns from musical director Mark Keith how its choir was saved ten years ago and is now thriving, partly due to an innovative partnership that takes music into local primary schools to spread the joy of singing. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita continues her east coast road trip, visiting the Naze, a nature reserve on the Essex coast. Here, coastal erosion is particularly severe, with around 2 to 3 metres lost from the cliffs every year. But there are benefits to a crumbling coastline – it can reveal 55 million years of history. Anita joins a group of enthusiastic fossil hunters on the lookout for remnants of the coast's fascinating past. She also discovers what has been done to protect the area’s heritage and visits one of over a thousand brightly coloured beach huts overlooking the North Sea. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the hidden histories found across our landscape.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Paramedics are mobilised to a large building fire in Glasgow City Centre, with concerns that people are trapped inside. As a PRU - or Paramedic Response Unit - Stewart is often deployed to some of the ambulance service’s most urgent emergencies. As fire and rescue battle the blaze, Stewart endures heavy rain and prepares to treat casualties. Meanwhile, Ayr-based crew Sophie and Shelby treat a man who has been drinking alcohol and gotten injured in a fall. He has sustained a concerning head injury but is adamant he doesn’t want to go to hospital. For Sophie and Shelby, who want to take the patient to a place of safety, it’s a frustrating situation that is one of around 20,000 alcohol-related calls that the ambulance service attends every year. In Glasgow’s Ambulance Control Centre, Fraser takes a difficult 999 call from a woman who is threatening to harm herself following the breakdown of her relationship. Fraser is able to draw on his own mental health experiences to help comfort the caller while further help is arranged. And in Perth, teammates Keara and Ashleigh help Keith, who is undergoing cancer treatment and showing worrying signs of an infection.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. The local park has gone downhill, and Winston has a plan that will improve it.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Fighting the lawless and ensuring the law wins. Volunteer officer Ken Beattie wrestles with a dodgy dealer and the dilemma of whether that dealer is or isn't offering him a bribe. Officer Karen is in the middle of something and has no time whatsoever for whatever Bobby wants to bother her about - even if it involves a famous face recognising a community hero. Party animals go wild in the country as Charlie introduces Jane to the etiquette surrounding the rural festival known as the Butterfist. And the Chief pushes his professional productivity to the max as he receives an open razor shave at his desk. Starring Jack Docherty, James Allenby-Kirk, Karen Bartke, Darren Connell, Chris Forbes, Ashley Smith and special guest Shereen Nanjiani.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Animation. It’s 1995, and welcome to Dave’s Games: your one-stop shop for all things video games, from computers and consoles to poppers and Pogs - and how can you forget the floor-to-ceiling piles of plastic game cartridges? Self-appointed ‘gaming legend’, shop owner and father (in that order), Dave is the king of his own crumbling kingdom. Sure, there is mould on the ceiling and some of the oldest video games you’ve ever seen (even for 1995), but it’s the only games shop in town. At least until the gigantic, shiny, futuristic rival shop Turbo Gamez opens just down the road. And they also happen to be releasing the newest and most sophisticated piece of gaming technology the world has ever seen: the first PlayStation…

But will they reach her in time, and can they stop an uprising before it is too late?

programme.desc: Best friends Evie and Noa have watched films together since they first met at university. programme.desc: Animation. Self-appointed ‘gaming legend’, shop owner and father (in that order), Dave is the king of his own crumbling kingdom. Sure, there is mould on the ceiling and some of the oldest video games you’ve ever seen (even for 1995), but it’s the only games shop in town. At least until the gigantic, shiny, futuristic rival shop Turbo Gamez opens just down the road. And they also happen to be releasing the newest and most sophisticated piece of gaming technology the world has ever seen: the first PlayStation…

But will they reach her in time, and can they stop an uprising before it is too late?

programme.title: Madonna at the BBC
programme.desc: A look back at a selection of magical Madonna moments on various BBC shows, from her first Top of the Pops appearance with Holiday in 1984 right up to the present day. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Ruth Madeley unearths a long-buried family secret about an adoption, and a mystery that requires DNA testing and meticulous genealogical detective work to uncover a lost ancestor.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, she's exploring subjects that all begin with the letter P. Programmes include: Gardeners' World, The One Show, RHS Chelsea Flower Show, Grow Your Own Veg and Flora Britannica. With presenters: Alys Fowler, Mike Dilger, Rachel de Thame, Christine Walkden, Monty Don, Laurence Llewellyn-Bowen and Carol Klein.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden is in the air above two glorious Gloucestershire gardens. At Hidcote Manor Garden she cuts an underperforming shrub down to size and meets Sue, for whom the garden is an inspiration. At Kiftsgate Court Gardens she tackles an enormous rambling rose. We discover the arts and crafts heritage of the Cotswolds.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The next stop on Anita's road trip is West Mersea in Essex. While the county may be known for engineering and car manufacturing, along its coastline one industry has a much longer history. Oysters have been harvested here for more than 2,000 years, cultivated in the creeks around Mersea Island. Over the decades, oyster farming has adapted to changing environmental conditions and the arrival of the non-native Pacific rock oyster. To experience what oyster harvesting is like today, Anita heads onto the brackish waters to meet the people farming oysters. She also meets the team investigating how the non-native Pacific rock oyster is affecting the local ecosystem and whether it could play a role in helping coastal habitats respond to rising sea levels. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the people and projects shaping life around our coastline.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek goes island hopping, visiting Caldey off the Pembrokeshire coast, then Anglesey, known for its seabirds, before finishing in south Wales at Barry Island, his childhood home.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The weather in this year’s growing season is making gardening a real challenge at Beechgrove, with cold grey skies and periods of high temperature giving Ruth Vichos and Brian Cunningham plenty to deal with. Ruth is in her vertical garden, where she has strawberries, blossoms and various climbing varieties all demonstrating what you can produce if you are short of space, using stacking systems and plants that will follow vertical surfaces. Brian reviews the wildflower beds he sowed in April, which will become a great resource for pollinators and the rest of the garden’s ecosystem. Brian and Ruth look at the diseases and pests that might be attacking your garden favourites right now and what to do about them. There is a visit to a great garden in East Lothian, and all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt celebrates the best of seasonal produce with the help of some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Bryn Williams puts courgettes centre stage by dressing them in a sharp and zesty citrus dressing and topping with a fillet of pan-fried sea bream. Meanwhile, Poppy O’Toole has three viral recipes – hot honey chicken, feta and pomegranate chopped salad and crispy smashed potato salad. Gennaro Contaldo tampers with an Italian classic, Ravneet Gill has a showstopping mango roulade with a creamy panna cotta filling, and Carmen O’Neal has a rundown of the best rums from around the world. Finally Vanessa Williams tucks into either her food heaven, butterflied bass with fries, or her food hell, pork and black bean tacos. Meanwhile, Rick Stein embarks on a moonlit fishing trip, and the Hairy Bikers hope to catch tuna in Sardinia.

programme.title: A Man for All Seasons
programme.desc: Multi-award-winning historical drama about Sir Thomas More's refusal to acknowledge Henry VIII's break with the Roman Catholic Church. King Henry VIII wants the pope to grant him a divorce from his barren wife to marry Anne Boleyn in order to get a male heir. Above all, he wants the endorsement of his newly appointed chancellor and widely respected scholar Sir Thomas More. But More has a divine conscience and will not consent to a break with the church of Rome. The scene is set for a struggle between the power of a king and a man who loves God more than his life. Paul Scofield's performance won one of the film's six Oscars, which also included the best picture award. Adapted by Robert Bolt from his own stage play.

programme.title: I Was Monty's Double
programme.desc: World War II drama. A low-ranking officer who resembles General Montgomery is recruited to play his double in an elaborate plan to trick the Nazis.

programme.title: GAA Live
programme.desc: Holly Hamilton presents live coverage of the All-Ireland Hurling final between Galway and Limerick from a sold-out Croke Park. It's one of the standout days in the Irish sporting calendar and is steeped in history, pride and fierce rivalry. Holly is joined in the studio by All-Ireland winners Paul Murphy and Séamus Flanagan, and Neil McManus. Mark Sidebottom provides pitch-side updates, with commentary by Thomas Niblock and Clare legend Jamesie O’Connor. Stars from the worlds of sport and entertainment are set to join the coverage for a special day in Irish sport.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and the Flog It! team are in Greater Manchester, where over 800 people come along to have their items valued at Stockport Town Hall. Paul is joined by experts Mark Stacey and Philip Serrell as they pick out their favourite antiques to take to auction. Mark is wowed by a William De Morgan ceramic tile, Paul finds some etchings by artist John Buckland Wright and Philip discovers a gold necklace that surprises everyone at auction.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Fiona and Philip unravel the mystery of a suspected Fabergé flower, kept hidden in a shoebox in Liverpool but believed to have belonged to royalty – and worth a small fortune!

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of the imposing Elizabethan mansion Wollaton Hall in Nottingham. Silver expert Kate Flitcroft is shaken, not stirred, by a stunning fire extinguisher cocktail shaker that turns up, while ceramics expert Eric Knowles meets his match with a cheeky toy monkey popping out of a musical pineapple. Fiona Bruce arrives in style on an iconic Chopper bike and tells the story of Raleigh Bicycles, founded in Nottingham in the 1880s. She learns about local activist George Powe, who campaigned to secure employment opportunities for black workers at Raleigh in the 1950s, and hears from two former employees about life inside what was once the world’s largest bicycle factory. Jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt challenges Fiona to guess the value of three intriguing cameo items, and collectables expert Hilary Kay is surprised to discover some of Queen Victoria’s personal undergarments with a sizeable price tag to boot.

programme.title: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society
programme.desc: In London, 1946, author Juliet Ashton's career has taken off, but she is not enjoying promoting her detective stories to eager audiences on a book tour. When she receives a letter from a Guernsey pig farmer inviting her to attend a meeting of his literary society, she eagerly accepts. What Juliet discovers about her new friends and their secrets leads to her staying on the island much longer than she planned.

programme.title: Golf: The Open
programme.desc: Highlights from the final day of the 154th Open as the Champion Golfer of the Year is crowned at Royal Birkdale. Previous winners at the famous Southport links include Arnold Palmer, Tom Watson, Padraig Harrington and Jordan Spieth, who secured a dramatic victory when the Claret Jug was last won here back in 2017. World number one Scottie Scheffler started the week as defending champion following his emphatic triumph at Royal Portrush in 2025, with world number two Rory McIlroy hoping to bookend his major season with a Claret Jug to add to the Green Jacket he won at the Masters in April.

programme.title: ODI Cricket
programme.desc: Highlights from the third ODI of 2026 between England and India.

programme.title: Margrete: Queen of the North
programme.desc: Powerful and tense historical epic about the untold story of the woman who united Scandinavia in a time of war. The year is 1402. Margrete has achieved what no man has managed before: she has gathered Denmark, Norway and Sweden into a peace-oriented union that she rules through her adopted son, King Erik. But a conspiracy is in the making, and Margrete finds herself in an impossible dilemma that could shatter her life’s work.

programme.title: Countryfile

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The weather in this year’s growing season is making gardening a real challenge at Beechgrove, with cold grey skies and periods of high temperature giving Ruth Vichos and Brian Cunningham plenty to deal with. Ruth is in her vertical garden, where she has strawberries, blossoms and various climbing varieties all demonstrating what you can produce if you are short of space, using stacking systems and plants that will follow vertical surfaces. Brian reviews the wildflower beds he sowed in April, which will become a great resource for pollinators and the rest of the garden’s ecosystem. Brian and Ruth look at the diseases and pests that might be attacking your garden favourites right now and what to do about them. There is a visit to a great garden in East Lothian, and all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt celebrates the best of seasonal produce with the help of some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Bryn Williams puts courgettes centre stage by dressing them in a sharp and zesty citrus dressing and topping with a fillet of pan-fried sea bream. Meanwhile, Poppy O’Toole has three viral recipes – hot honey chicken, feta and pomegranate chopped salad and crispy smashed potato salad. Gennaro Contaldo tampers with an Italian classic, Ravneet Gill has a showstopping mango roulade with a creamy panna cotta filling, and Carmen O’Neal has a rundown of the best rums from around the world. Finally Vanessa Williams tucks into either her food heaven, butterflied bass with fries, or her food hell, pork and black bean tacos. Meanwhile, Rick Stein embarks on a moonlit fishing trip, and the Hairy Bikers hope to catch tuna in Sardinia.

programme.title: A Man for All Seasons
programme.desc: Multi-award-winning historical drama about Sir Thomas More's refusal to acknowledge Henry VIII's break with the Roman Catholic Church. King Henry VIII wants the pope to grant him a divorce from his barren wife to marry Anne Boleyn in order to get a male heir. Above all, he wants the endorsement of his newly appointed chancellor and widely respected scholar Sir Thomas More. But More has a divine conscience and will not consent to a break with the church of Rome. The scene is set for a struggle between the power of a king and a man who loves God more than his life. Paul Scofield's performance won one of the film's six Oscars, which also included the best picture award. Adapted by Robert Bolt from his own stage play.

programme.title: I Was Monty's Double
programme.desc: World War II drama. A low-ranking officer who resembles General Montgomery is recruited to play his double in an elaborate plan to trick the Nazis.

programme.title: GAA Live
programme.desc: Holly Hamilton presents live coverage of the All-Ireland Hurling final between Galway and Limerick from a sold-out Croke Park. It's one of the standout days in the Irish sporting calendar and is steeped in history, pride and fierce rivalry. Holly is joined in the studio by All-Ireland winners Paul Murphy and Séamus Flanagan, and Neil McManus. Mark Sidebottom provides pitch-side updates, with commentary by Thomas Niblock and Clare legend Jamesie O’Connor. Stars from the worlds of sport and entertainment are set to join the coverage for a special day in Irish sport.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and the Flog It! team are in Greater Manchester, where over 800 people come along to have their items valued at Stockport Town Hall. Paul is joined by experts Mark Stacey and Philip Serrell as they pick out their favourite antiques to take to auction. Mark is wowed by a William De Morgan ceramic tile, Paul finds some etchings by artist John Buckland Wright and Philip discovers a gold necklace that surprises everyone at auction.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Fiona and Philip unravel the mystery of a suspected Fabergé flower, kept hidden in a shoebox in Liverpool but believed to have belonged to royalty – and worth a small fortune!

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of the imposing Elizabethan mansion Wollaton Hall in Nottingham. Silver expert Kate Flitcroft is shaken, not stirred, by a stunning fire extinguisher cocktail shaker that turns up, while ceramics expert Eric Knowles meets his match with a cheeky toy monkey popping out of a musical pineapple. Fiona Bruce arrives in style on an iconic Chopper bike and tells the story of Raleigh Bicycles, founded in Nottingham in the 1880s. She learns about local activist George Powe, who campaigned to secure employment opportunities for black workers at Raleigh in the 1950s, and hears from two former employees about life inside what was once the world’s largest bicycle factory. Jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt challenges Fiona to guess the value of three intriguing cameo items, and collectables expert Hilary Kay is surprised to discover some of Queen Victoria’s personal undergarments with a sizeable price tag to boot.

programme.title: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society
programme.desc: In London, 1946, author Juliet Ashton's career has taken off, but she is not enjoying promoting her detective stories to eager audiences on a book tour. When she receives a letter from a Guernsey pig farmer inviting her to attend a meeting of his literary society, she eagerly accepts. What Juliet discovers about her new friends and their secrets leads to her staying on the island much longer than she planned.

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and Conker are joined in their cooking den by Alex, a figure skater who wants a meal that will warm him and his friend up after training on the ice! Alex likes meat, but his friend is vegetarian, so he needs Buddy’s help with something that will keep them both happy... Buddy knows that burgers are a winner as they’re super-flexible, so he creates the ultimate burger for Alex that’s half beef mince and half lentils that his friend can swap for veggie mince and lentils. Using lentils also means you use less meat, which is good for you and the planet – win, win! In return, Alex takes Buddy to train on the ice, teaching him the skills to skate forwards, backwards, stop and build up some speed – and how to style it out when you fall over! It turns out that the key to good form is making lemons with your feet – so there’s more in common with the kitchen than Buddy thought! Join Buddy, Conker and Alex as they glide through the recipe and ice rink in a super-tasty episode of Cooking Buddies! You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food.

The rope breaks, and the kite flies off, causing mayhem in Fluffytown with everyone thinking it is a real dragon invasion. Finally, Elder Panda arrives and manages to bring it down to the ground using an umbrella, and Love Monster comes clean, saying how sorry he is. Elder Panda is disappointed, but he does understand, as he too wanted to fly before he could run. Sometimes, however, you have to start small before going big.

programme.title: Piggy Builders

programme.title: Roots and Fruits

programme.desc: Supertato, Carrot and Tomato are making friendship bracelets in the craft aisle, but this gives Evil Pea the crafty idea of making a monster costume to scare them all out of the supermarket. With herself and the Corn Cobs stacked on top of each other, they initially get the veggies to run away. Supertato wonders if the monster is just looking for a new friend, so he chases after it! When one of the arms falls off the monster, the Tato Team realise it’s just someone in a costume. They find out it was Evil Pea all along!

programme.desc: Bing and Sula are having so much fun playing together, they don't want to say goodbye when Amma arrives to pick Sula up. To delay her departure, Bing hides Sula's sparkly shoe in the toilet, and it gets soaking wet - much to Sula's annoyance. It looks as though Sula will have to hop home, until Bing finds a way to turn the 'bad-bye' back into a goodbye again.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing is teaching Charlie how to throw, but when he throws the ball in the lounge it knocks the fruit over! Bing starts to explain, but Charlie interrupts, leaving Flop to believe Charlie did it. Bing happily shows Charlie how to voosh Squeaky instead, but it flies out of his hands and hits Flop's tray of snacks! After some encouragement, Bing tells Flop the truth and apologises.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels hear an echoing voice coming from the top of a castle's spooky tower. Someone is calling them - but who is it? Duggee and the Squirrels go off to investigate, but first they have to get inside the castle. Good job Duggee knows how. Prepare to be taken on a huge chase around the castle before the Squirrels finally discover who is making all that mischief and noise at the top of the castle.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee has something really interesting to show the Squirrels but it's a bit prickly. The Squirrels go off into the garden to find their own interesting things to show and tell, and they all make very different choices. Norrie finds a very special creature with six spots. Can you guess what it is?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Jerry Lee, the chief scientist in the dream house is onboarding a new butler.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are going to Westman Islands, Iceland, where the world’s largest colony of Atlantic puffins gathers every year. Lars loves these tough little birds and explains how, although they spend most of their lives flying out to sea and fishing, they return to land each year to lay their eggs. When the baby birds, also called pufflings, eventually hatch, they fly out towards the ocean. But the light from nearby towns often confuses them about where to go, leading local children and adults to form 'puffin patrols' to rescue the pufflings. Lars is excited to help out but is upset when he discovers Glitch, also a fan of puffins, is already well-known on the islands for his skills as a puffin rescuer. Although Glitch offers him a place in his puffin patrol, Lars is determined to outdo Glitch with a patrol of his own - but when he recruits a clumsy Grimbot, things take a turn for the worse...

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: When Peso's precious medical kit is taken, Barnacles and Kwazii sneak into a dangerous walrus - disguised as a walrus! - to get it back.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: As Mum goes for a walk along the beach, Bluey runs to catch up with her. Along the way, she has a series of encounters that both excite and test her in her first solo adventure.

programme.title: Bluey

Happy got a new bath sponge, Norrie is growing a sunflower and Roly, after thinking hard if he’s got any news at all, remembers he’s getting a new brother or sister. The Squirrels have all sorts of questions to ask.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are playing outside, when out of a bush jumps the cutest creature they ever did see. They think it is simply adorable and tell it so… with startling results. The creature bursts into tears! The creature, whose name is Plinky, tells them her whole family are monsters, and that’s what she’s supposed to be, but she just cannot get the hang of it. The Squirrels are keen to help Plinky get in touch with her scary side. Fortunately, Duggee has his monster badge.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: When Gadabout and Pearl lose the cure for Madam Dragon’s missing flame, Zog helps them work together to assist his former teacher.

programme.desc: Nugget arranges an ice-sculpting event, but only Flutter turns up. However, when his tongue gets accidentally stuck to the ice, it takes the whole colony to solve the problem.

With a mischievous idea and a little magic, Rafi wishes they could switch places. When the wish wears off, Rafi realises that some things are best enjoyed when you’re exactly who you’re meant to be.

programme.desc: Dad drops an essential gizmo in a hard-to-reach place. Big Lizard takes them on an underwater adventure to meet Ammon, the tentacled solution to their problem!

programme.desc: Silver Paw 'turtlenaps' Moss - can Jeremy and Deena find her before the school run?

programme.desc: Weasy shows off his pedal car. The ducklings want to try it out, but Weasy refuses because they are too small. The ducklings see an experiment on the Farm of the Future that could solve their problem: a device that makes you grow!

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Tom throws a dumpster into space to impress the others, but what goes up must come down.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of singing potatoes. The Small Potatoes sing about the importance of family and friends in this heartfelt ballad.

programme.desc: No, Rebecca isn’t wearing a box on her head - she’s dressed as an astronaut! This gives Murphi an idea. He helps Rebecca discover alien life by creating an alien out of a sock. The Mini Monsters are making skyscapes, Rebecca’s royal relative is looking for something, and the final mega monster make is another space-inspired creation. The Recycling Express and the Tiny Helpers support Rebecca and Murphi as they reach for the stars.

programme.desc: Naima's family are from Algeria. Naima is cooking a special Algerian borek for her friends to try. Borek is made from pastry, mashed potato, meat, cheese and olives. The great thing about borek is that you can add lots of different ingredients depending on what you like, and that's exactly what Naima is doing today. Naima mashes her potatoes, cuts some spring onions and sprinkles in some cinnamon before she gets the table ready for her Algerian feast. Naima's friends are not sure about the taste of cinnamon when they try it first, but will they like it cooked in her recipe? Let's hope so!

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa

We meet some children from a beach club in Scotland who are combing the sand to help the wildlife and we find out how a farmer in Wales turns goats’ milk into soap. Storm shares a summer poem.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee has made a beautiful rock pool, a place of calm for all the animals. The Squirrels spot the strangest things - dots with tails, wriggling around. What on earth are they? They are baby frogs - tadpoles! But they don't sound or look like Frog.

programme.desc: The Go Jetters join Ubercorn in the Go Jet Academy to try out a brand new click-on: the GO Vac, a supervacuum that can suck up bad weather. In order to put it to the test, Ubercorn creates a small hailstorm cloud inside the dome and Lars tries to suck it up with the GO Vac. However, Glitch appears and tries to show off his new 'Grim-o-Freeze' and zaps the cloud. Instead of disappearing, it grows in size and ferocity, breaking the roof with a smash. The sudden change in pressure blows everyone about inside the dome and the cloud blows outside, taking Glitch and the Grimbots with it. The Go Jetters need to catch it fast so launch their brand new vehicle, the Truckster.

programme.title: Big Lizard

programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he does not hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel is Rayane’s ears. Together, they are unstoppable! Rayane is playing the detective in the drama club play, and Diesel is going to be right by his side as his trusty police dog. At the theatre, Diesel helps Rayane and his friend Grace practise for something called a 'cue' - their big moment to go on stage. Diesel must give Rayane a nudge when he hears two rings from a big red telephone. But during the show, someone’s phone goes off in the audience! Can Diesel save the day and make sure that Rayane takes to the stage at the right time?

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Peas help a furry friend learn a new skill.

programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar drive through the baboons’ enclosure in a special bus. The mischievous baboons have fun climbing all over the bus and show off their acrobatic skills. It’s then feeding time for the giant river otters, who show Steve and Aneeshwar their super swimming skills. They then find out the wild connection between these two very different animals.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: After an emotional farewell to their home and family in the UK, Becky and the kids make the big move to Italy, taking everything with them - including their dogs and grand piano. But Italian life is immediately complicated, with a frustrated Jamie injured and unable to play but desperate to start scoring goals for his new club. The kids love their new Italian home but struggle being away from friends - will Becky and Jamie's grand plans for Sofia's birthday be enough to take her mind off friends back home? With Jamie's punishing training schedule taking its toll, he doesn't get as much time with the family as he'd like, leaving Becky to help them settle in and do her best to source home comforts for the kids - but she can't find baked beans or orange squash anywhere. Still, Jamie makes time for some magic family moments, and the family begin to find their feet, learning the language, experiencing the culture and Jamie makes his much-awaited debut on the pitch with explosive results.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: It's a day of busy appointments for Fern Britton today at The Grove Vets in Bristol. She meets Louie, a Jack Russell terrier whose enormous lump is proving to be a puzzle for the vets, and a 10-month-old kitten is brought in with an injury obtained in a fight. Dr James Greenwood provides emergency care to a whippet with a nasty throat injury, and also delivers a masterclass on doggy dental hygiene with special help from his own pooch, Dolly. Veterinary surgeon Andy demonstrates one of the latest techniques for canine corn removal to help a rescue greyhound with a painful foot pad, and we get an insight into what it takes to become a vet at Bristol Veterinary School.

But Italian life is immediately complicated, with a frustrated Jamie injured and unable to play but desperate to start scoring goals for his new club. The kids love their new Italian home but struggle being away from friends - will Becky and Jamie's grand plans for Sofia's birthday be enough to take her mind off friends back home? With Jamie's punishing training schedule taking its toll, he doesn't get as much time with the family as he'd like, leaving Becky to help them settle in and do her best to source home comforts for the kids - but she can't find baked beans or orange squash anywhere. Still, Jamie makes time for some magic family moments, and the family begin to find their feet, learning the language, experiencing the culture and Jamie makes his much-awaited debut on the pitch with explosive results.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: After an emotional farewell to their home and family in the UK, Becky and the kids make the big move to Italy, taking everything with them - including their dogs and grand piano. But Italian life is immediately complicated, with a frustrated Jamie injured and unable to play but desperate to start scoring goals for his new club. The kids love their new Italian home but struggle being away from friends - will Becky and Jamie's grand plans for Sofia's birthday be enough to take her mind off friends back home? With Jamie's punishing training schedule taking its toll, he doesn't get as much time with the family as he'd like, leaving Becky to help them settle in and do her best to source home comforts for the kids - but she can't find baked beans or orange squash anywhere. Still, Jamie makes time for some magic family moments, and the family begin to find their feet, learning the language, experiencing the culture and Jamie makes his much-awaited debut on the pitch with explosive results.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: After an emotional farewell to their home and family in the UK, Becky and the kids make the big move to Italy, taking everything with them - including their dogs and grand piano. But Italian life is immediately complicated, with a frustrated Jamie injured and unable to play but desperate to start scoring goals for his new club. The kids love their new Italian home but struggle being away from friends - will Becky and Jamie's grand plans for Sofia's birthday be enough to take her mind off friends back home? With Jamie's punishing training schedule taking its toll, he doesn't get as much time with the family as he'd like, leaving Becky to help them settle in and do her best to source home comforts for the kids - but she can't find baked beans or orange squash anywhere. Still, Jamie makes time for some magic family moments, and the family begin to find their feet, learning the language, experiencing the culture and Jamie makes his much-awaited debut on the pitch with explosive results.

programme.desc: It's a day of busy appointments for Fern Britton today at The Grove Vets in Bristol. She meets Louie, a Jack Russell terrier whose enormous lump is proving to be a puzzle for the vets, and a 10-month-old kitten is brought in with an injury obtained in a fight. Dr James Greenwood provides emergency care to a whippet with a nasty throat injury, and also delivers a masterclass on doggy dental hygiene with special help from his own pooch, Dolly. Veterinary surgeon Andy demonstrates one of the latest techniques for canine corn removal to help a rescue greyhound with a painful foot pad, and we get an insight into what it takes to become a vet at Bristol Veterinary School.

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: Jack the Ripper. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Niall MacGinnis & Dorothy Alison. A troubled clairvoyant dreams of Jack the Ripper's killings and assists the police. [S]

programme.title: Mickey One
programme.desc: 1965. Crime. Directed by Arthur Penn. Stars Warren Beatty, Alexandra Stewart & Hurd Hatfield. A stand-up comic incurs the wrath of the Mafia and escapes to Chicago but yearns to go back on stage. [S]

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: Italian saxophonist Riccardo Rauchi and his ensemble of musicians perform Okay Madison.

programme.title: The Adventures of Sir Lancelot
programme.desc: Thieves. 1957. Stars William Russell, Cyril Smith & Ronald Leigh-Hunt. It's difficult to find employment if branded a thief. Lancelot gets the King to don a disguise and enter a den of thieves. [S]

programme.title: Honey West
programme.desc: 1965. Like Visions and Omens and All That Jazz. Classic crime series produced by Aaron Spelling and starring Anne Francis. A psychic predicts several murder attempts on an heiress.

programme.title: A Tale of Five Cities
programme.desc: 1951. Drama. Stars Bonar Colleano, Barbara Kelly, Eva Bartok & Gina Lollobrigida. An Englishman leaves America to enlist in the RAF, but a drunken accident results in a loss of memory. [S]

programme.title: Fate Takes a Hand
programme.desc: 1961. Drama. Director: Max Varnel. Stars Ronald Howard, Christina Gregg, Basil Dignam. Letters recovered from a stolen mail bag significantly impact the lives of the recipients 15 years later. [S]

programme.title: The Drum
programme.desc: 1938. War. Directed by Zoltan Korda. Stars Sabu, Raymond Massey & Roger Livesey. When the Khan of Tokot is murdered, his killer, the evil Prince Ghul, plots an uprising against British rule. [S]

programme.title: Batman
programme.desc: The Bloody Tower. 1967. Stars Adam West, Burt Ward & Glynis Johns. Batman saves Robin & Batgirl. Robin is stung by a Death Bee. Lord Ffogg & Lady Peasoup prepare to steal the crown jewels. [S]

programme.title: For Those In Peril
programme.desc: 1944. War Drama. Director: Charles Crichton. Stars David Farrar, Ralph Michael & Robert Wyndham. A WWII flyer fails to join the RAF so he joins the Air - Sea Rescue instead. [S]

programme.title: Pollyanna
programme.desc: 2002. Drama. Directed by Sarah Harding. Stars Amanda Burton, Tom Bell & Kenneth Cranham. Young orphan Pollyanna, bringing mirth and mayhem to her new home, goes to stay with her Aunt Polly. [S]

programme.title: Dial 999
programme.desc: 77 Bus. 1958. Stars Robert Beatty, Robert Cawdron & Ivan Craig. Police are baffled by robberies known as 'the Red Rose series'; Maguire and his partner suspect a seemingly innocent jeweller. [S]

programme.title: For the Love of Ada
programme.desc: Another Man. 1970. Stars Wilfred Pickles, Irene Handl & Jack Smethurst. Walter's refusal to go dancing at the Over 60s Club and acceptance of overcooked pies from other women annoys Ada. (S1, E05) [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: Alexander the Great Affair: Part One. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum & Leo G. Carroll. A mysterious U.S. industrialist, Mr. Alexander, steals a new type of nerve gas from the U.S. Army. [S]

programme.title: The Footage Detectives
programme.desc: Take a trip in the past lane with a nostalgic cycling proficiency film featuring a young Roy Hudd, a lost training film starring John Cleese & Adrienne Posta, & a reminisce on teatime traditions. [S]

programme.title: The Winslow Boy
programme.desc: 1948. Drama. Directed by Anthony Asquith. Stars Robert Donat, Cedric Hardwicke & Basil Radford. Pre-WWI England, a youngster is expelled from a naval academy for theft. His parents demand a trial. [S]

programme.title: Francis Durbridge's...
programme.desc: ... A Game of Murder. 1966. Stars Gerald Harper, Conrad Phillips & David Burke. When a former athlete's mysterious death seems suspicious, his detective son investigates. [S]

programme.title: Horror of Frankenstein
programme.desc: 1971. Horror. Directed by Jimmy Sangster. Stars Dennis Price, Kate O'Mara & Ralph Bates. Young Victor Frankenstein inherits his father's title, his castle and his taste for grisly experiments. [S]

programme.title: Night of the Big Heat
programme.desc: 1967. Sci-Fi. Directed by Terence Fisher. Starring Christopher Lee, Peter Cushing & Patrick Allen. A heatwave forces the atmosphere to boil. It falls on Godfrey Hanson to discover the reason. [S]

programme.desc: After an emotional farewell to their home and family in the UK, Becky and the kids make the big move to Italy, taking everything with them - including their dogs and grand piano. But Italian life is immediately complicated, with a frustrated Jamie injured and unable to play but desperate to start scoring goals for his new club. The kids love their new Italian home but struggle being away from friends - will Becky and Jamie's grand plans for Sofia's birthday be enough to take her mind off friends back home? With Jamie's punishing training schedule taking its toll, he doesn't get as much time with the family as he'd like, leaving Becky to help them settle in and do her best to source home comforts for the kids - but she can't find baked beans or orange squash anywhere.
